_comment: The static RAM (.data and .bss) that the objects under src/ui/angulo define, a high-water mark in the manner of flash_budget.json. tools/check_ui_ram.py adds it up from the objdump -t listing of each object after every build (what counts is decided by section, .bss* and .data*, not by nm's letter, which calls a weak read-only table a variable) of an image that carries the Angulo and holds the total to "budget" exactly: growing past it is allowed, doing so without editing it in the same change is not, and a build that shrinks lowers it in the same change (a budget that only rises stops measuring). The heap pays for every byte: the telemetry batch drops to one entry below HEAP_RESERVE (TelemetryManager.cpp), 32,768 B with TLS telemetry. Padding between objects is not counted. An entry also bounds a configurator build (tools/build_custom.py, the _custom environment) that names it in custom_ui_ram_budget_env, as a ceiling and not as an exact mark: under it passes, over it fails, and raising the entry raises that ceiling for the configurator too.
measured_on: 2026-10-16 perf/ui-angulo-2canais: 9,313 B (b9d9b37, same method: 9,205 B). 2026-10-21 s10b/c0b: pico2_w_angulo joins at 9,313 B in 33 objects, measured by the gate itself in the build of the RP2350 image (the Wire Angulo's number, the same objects). 2026-10-22 s10c/a2: 9,603 B in both Angulo images (+290 B): the palette's twelve resident tables of 36 B (six accents x two modes, built before Core 1 starts and only read) where four stood; the heap pays, byte for byte. 2026-10-22 s10c/a2b: 9,171 B in both Angulo images (-432 B): the generator emits the tables constexpr, the palette is built by the compiler and kept in flash, and the static initialiser that filled it is gone. 2026-10-22 s10c/b2b: 9,175 B in both Angulo images (+4 B): the pointer to the published table of texts (Textos.cpp). The glue's first version logged from its own function and the check read 9,695 B: LOG_CODE( ) instantiates LogManager::instance( ), whose function-local singleton (516 B and a 4 B guard) is a weak variable the check counts once for the Angulo's objects, and the image has it from LogManager.cpp anyway; the hook now returns the reason and the core logs it (AppManager_Boot.cpp)
